history.summary: Pilgrimage shrine on the east side of Bharuch at Dandia Bazar, on the banks of the Narmada, dedicated to the sage Bhrigu. Bharuch's ancient name Bhrigukachchha is said to derive from this temple. Tradition holds Bhrigu's ashram stood here and that he wrote the Bhrigu Samhita (Indian astrology work) at this spot; he is said to have narrated the Ganesh Purana to King Somakanta here. The current structure, built by the Marathas between 1675 and 1686 CE, is divided into two parts: one housing newly carved idols of Bhrigu, Jamadagni, Renuka, Parashurama and Ganesha, and the core section with Narayana, the four Vedas as Shiva lingas, Dashavatara idols, and Jwaleshwar Mahadev worshipped by the rishi. CSV STATE FLAG: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name - this temple is in GUJARAT (Bharuch district).

town_description: Bharuch is an ancient river-port city on the Narmada in south Gujarat, among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in India (ancient Bhrigukachchha). It is a district headquarters and a major industrial hub, dotted with ghats and old temples along the river.
